scenes.say: A wallet can build years of perfect repayment history on Ethereum, and still arrive on any other chain as a complete stranger.

Moving that record is the easy half. Making it trustworthy is the hard half — a signature proves key control, a bridge asks you to trust a committee, and an oracle puts back the middleman you were removing.
So Hana imports the record and has Creditcoin verify it on chain — a Merkle inclusion proof checked by the Attestcoin precompile. The result is one public view call that any contract can read.

And a registry only one app reads is just plumbing. So there are two, deliberately different — retail buy-now-pay-later, and a DePIN node operator credit line — on the same score, with no coupling between them.
This is Hana — a cross-chain credit primitive on Creditcoin. The whole integration surface is one view call: getCreditLimit, for any address and any asset.
Nothing here is a mockup. Every contract is deployed and verified on Creditcoin's CC3 testnet, and this page reads the addresses straight from the deployment record.
Here's the checkout app, with a wallet connected that has a real repayment history — but that history is on Ethereum, not on Creditcoin.

And there's the score — seven eighty six. That number was not seeded here. It came from fourteen completed loans and forty on-time payments on Ethereum Sepolia, proved onto Creditcoin by a Merkle inclusion proof and verified by a precompile. No oracle signed off on it.

And this is the point of a primitive. One score, two completely unrelated credit products — retail buy-now-pay-later in iUSDC, and a DePIN node operator credit line in SPACE. Same registry, no coupling.
Let me actually spend it. Here's a demo storefront — I'll add a pair of headphones to the cart.
Open the cart, and check out with Hana.
Four instalments, underwritten against the imported limit. This is a real transaction — it's being signed and broadcast to CC3 right now.
The loan is live on chain — four instalments, the first one due, and the money already moved into the settlement vault.
Now the second product, on the same wallet and the same score. A credit line in SPACE, drawn and staked, that repays itself out of staking yield instead of my capital.
Claiming that yield pays the debt down. Again — real transaction, real staking yield, real block.
Two applications, one registry, and the interface is public. Any contract on Creditcoin can underwrite against this today — no partnership, no permission, no oracle subscription.
